messages.author: 447e2f2c316a6cae
messages.subject: Error estimating fitIndices()
parts:
Hi,

After obtaining a bi-factor model by bfactor() I try to compute the fit indices with no success. I get this message:

Internal matricies are very large and computations will therefore take an extended amount of time and require large amounts of RAM. The largest matrix has 63371 columns. Do you wish to continue anyways?
(yes/no): yes
Error: cannot allocate vector of size 29.9 Gb


The thing is, I have extended the memory limit up to 5e+11, and still get the same error message. The model estimated is composed by 5 specific factor plus the general one, and based on a 473x60 matrix. It converged after 216 iterations.

Thanks in advance!

Regina G Velázquez.

messages.subject: Re: Error estimating fitIndices()
parts:
The fitIndicies function still needs to be optimized a bit more for
larger datasets, and is not as of yet optimal for bifactor/two-tier
models. I'll look into it sometime in the near future, and thanks for
the report.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Error estimating fitIndices()
parts:
I've updated the development version to provide better accuracy for the M2 in bifactor models (and in general), but I don't think it will solve your issue. The problem is that there are a huge number of first and second-order moments that need to be accounted for, and in your case a dense matrix of size 63371 x 63371 has to be inverted....which is no simple task for any personal computer.

I've added an experimental feature to further collapse the tables based on some work by Cai, L. & Hansen, M. Limited-information goodness-of-fit testing of hierarchical item factor models. British Journal of Mathematical and Statistical Psychology, 2013, 66, 245-276, but for some reason it doesn't appear to behave well, and causes non-pd matrices. Pull requests are welcome if someone can hunt down what is going on here, since collapsing cells for graded response models will almost certainly solve this issue.

Phil
